reason: The service sorts order.items directly, changing the order's state from outside the Order class instead of through its own methods.
The service imports OrderRepository and creates a default one when none is injected, instead of only using the collaborator passed to its constructor.
Extracting the factor into a private helper inside PercentDiscount keeps the discount computed by the injected strategy.
Reordering the AppConfig.instance() branches keeps a single shared instance, so the singleton is unchanged.
Replacing the truthiness check with len(...) == 0 is an idiom change that keeps the same handler flow and delegation.
The handler computes the total with sum() and no longer delegates to the order service, bypassing the service layer for placing orders.
The handler reaches the repository through the service's private _repository attribute, which requirement 1 forbids explicitly.
Passing the total as a keyword argument to the injected discount strategy changes only call style, not the architecture.
The service calls order.items.extend(prices), mutating the order's items directly and skipping Order.add, instead of changing the order through its methods.
EventBus.publish slices the listener list to its first element, so not every subscribed listener is called as the observer contract requires.
